requirements.text: A declaration MUST be published and retrieved over HTTPS.
A consumer MAY also process a `200 OK` response whose `Content-Type` is `application/json` as a declaration; a response carrying any other media type is not a declaration.
A server MAY support the query parameters `target`, `start`, `end`, and `granularity`, carried in the query component of the URI ({{RFC3986}}, Section 3.4) in name=value form.

Because a server may ignore any parameter, a consumer MUST compare the `period` and `target` of every object it receives with what it requested, and MUST NOT record a response as covering a period or a target it does not name.
An object's `period` and `target` say what it covers; figures covering part of a target or part of a period MUST NOT be presented as though they covered the whole.
A single object is equivalent to a one-object array, and a consumer MUST accept both forms.
A publisher MUST NOT add a top-level member this document does not define; other data goes in `extensions` ({{extensions}}).

A consumer ignores a top-level member it does not recognize and MUST NOT treat its presence as an error ({{RFC7493}}, Section 4.2); this document defines no version member, since the media type identifies the format.
**period** (object): The period the object covers, from `start`, included, to `end`, excluded, each an {{RFC3339}} `date-time`; `start` MUST be before `end`.
Bounds at midnight UTC, written with `Z`, are RECOMMENDED.
Whole calendar years and months are RECOMMENDED, being the periods reports state and consumers compare.
A period SHOULD be one or more whole calendar days: a shorter one can tie figures to individual requests ({{privacy-considerations}}), and whole days compare like for like.
It is an opaque protocol element: it MUST NOT be translated or transliterated, and is compared as a string.

For an organization its name is used; for an origin-wide report the origin's host (for example `"example.com"`) is RECOMMENDED; a path prefix is written like `"/api/v1"`; `target-type` classifies the other kinds.

Unless stated otherwise, a numeric member MUST NOT be negative, and a publisher MUST NOT emit a number whose magnitude or precision exceeds what IEEE 754 binary64 represents ({{RFC7493}}, Section 2.2).
Where they accompany `carbon-footprint` for the same period they SHOULD account for it; scopes that cover only part of that figure are explained in the methodology document.
These MAY be negative where the declared accounting method conveys removals or net figures, which the methodology document then explains.
**sci-score** (number): Software Carbon Intensity {{GSF-SCI}}, in grams of CO2e per `functional-unit`, which MUST then be present.

A declaration object MUST carry at least one numeric metric member or at least one of `disclosure-uri` and `verifiable-attestation-uri`; a metric not reported is omitted, and there is no in-band "not reported" value.
A consumer that implements a name's definition processes its value; a consumer that does not ignores the value and MUST NOT automatically dereference or execute anything within it.

The `upstream` member is an array of at least one object, each with a `declaration` member, a URI reference to that provider's declaration, and an OPTIONAL `role` member, one of `hosting`, `colocation`, `cloud`, `cdn`, `network`, and `electricity`, for those six kinds of provider; an entry for any other provider has no `role`.

The JOSE Header MUST contain `alg` naming an asymmetric digital-signature algorithm; `Ed25519` ({{RFC9864}}, with the key representation of {{RFC8037}}) and `ES256` ({{RFC7518}}, Section 3.4) are RECOMMENDED, and `none` and MAC algorithms MUST NOT be used, since a consumer shares no secret with the publisher.
The header MUST also contain `cty` ({{RFC7515}}, Section 4.1.10) with the value `sustainability-data+json`, which distinguishes it from a JWS made for another purpose.

The header SHOULD carry the verification key as `jwk` or `x5c`, so that verification needs nothing but the declaration; a publisher that distributes its key out of band MAY instead identify it with `kid`.

Retrieval establishes that the origin published these claims and nothing more: a consumer MUST NOT treat the presence of a declaration, or of any member in it, as verification of a claim, and one that presents, stores, or forwards the data MUST NOT represent it as verified.

A consumer that verifies `signed` MUST reject the member when `alg` is `none` or a MAC algorithm, when `cty` is absent or identifies any other media type, or when the header carries a `crit` parameter the consumer does not understand.

On success it reads the payload as a declaration object; a consumer MUST treat the object as unverified when the payload is not one or when the payload's `target`, `period.start`, `period.end`, `carbon-accounting`, or `functional-unit` differs from the object's.
Where an upstream publishes a `tenant` declaration about what it delivers to this target, a consumer MAY compare the two for the same period after conversion to one unit.
SHOULD bound the time, size, and redirects of every fetch, dereference only "https" references, and refuse a loopback, private, or link-local address at every connection it makes, redirects included;
MUST limit the bytes and objects it accepts and treat an excess as an error;

SHOULD parse with a JSON parser hardened against untrusted input ({{RFC8259}}, Section 12) and treat every value as data; one whose parser exposes duplicate member names SHOULD reject an object containing them;

that follows upstream declarations MUST NOT go deeper than three declarations below the one it started from, MUST refuse any URI it has already retrieved during the walk, and MUST bound the total number of retrievals in one walk.
A server that computes responses to query parameters on demand SHOULD rate-limit requests to the well-known URI and SHOULD cache what it computes.
A period shorter than a calendar day, which {{mandatory-members}} recommends against, can tie figures to individual requests; real-time telemetry is NOT RECOMMENDED.
A publisher MAY perturb the published values by multiplicative noise within 1% of the true values to blunt hardware fingerprinting.
A publisher SHOULD aggregate or omit any metric that could be linked to individual users or small groups, and SHOULD use a role rather than a personal contact address in `provider`.
A server that honors `start`, `end`, or `granularity` and receives a value not matching the ABNF ignores the parameter and never reads it as another value.
A server that does not support a parameter ignores it and answers the rest of the request; a static file therefore satisfies every request.

A server that supports these parameters returns the objects it holds that satisfy every parameter it honors, as a JSON array in ascending order of `period.start`, compared as instants; when none does, the array is empty. An object satisfies `start` and `end` when its period overlaps the range they bound: its `period.start` is before `end` and its `period.end` after `start`, as instants; an absent bound is unbounded.

It satisfies `target` when its `target` member equals the value, compared as {{mandatory-members}} says, and `granularity` when its period is a whole calendar year, month, or day, for `yearly`, `monthly`, or `daily` respectively ({{mandatory-members}}).

Human-readable identification of the publisher in any script, such as a name and a role contact address; a publisher that states its language does so with the `Content-Language` header field ({{RFC9110}}, Section 8.5), which applies to the whole response.

Where `target-type` is `origin` or the value is otherwise a host name, an internationalized host is written in A-label form ({{RFC5890}}, Section 2.3.2.1), and the host is compared case-insensitively ({{RFC3986}}, Section 3.2.2).
An object carries at most one; an index of further attestations is linked from `disclosure-uri`.

A consumer that wants a total adds `energy-consumption`, `carbon-footprint`, and the scope members, after conversion to one unit, across objects for one `target` whose periods do not overlap and that declare the same `carbon-accounting` value or none; two periods that meet, one's `end` being the next one's `start`, do not overlap.
